items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid scrutiny over personal relationships
items.summary: Huang resigned as president, CEO, and board member effective immediately, per an Nvidia SEC 8-K filing, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Reporting ties the departure to allegations of extramarital relationships, including one involving a suspected foreign intelligence contact, and Nvidia shares fell sharply before paring losses; the story is significant given Nvidia's central role in the AI buildout.
items.source: NBC News / CNBC / CNN / Al Jazeera

items.headline: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow ahead of planned Nasdaq listing
items.summary: Anthropic formally launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock, aiming to list on Nasdaq under the ticker 'ANT' with pricing expected around November 18. The move follows its October S-1 filing disclosing rapid revenue growth alongside large accounting-related losses, marking one of the largest AI-sector IPOs to date.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 for humanoid partners
items.summary: DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2.5, described as its most capable vision-language-action model yet, expanding the range and speed of skills robots can learn. The model is rolling out to robotics partners including Apptronik, Agile Robots, and Boston Dynamics, with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz reportedly testing Apollo 2 humanoids on an active auto production line.

items.headline: Google unveils TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max chips for the 'agentic era'
items.summary: Google Cloud introduced two new eighth-generation TPUs: 8tx, aimed at secure/confidential inference and small-scale training, and 8i Max, which doubles compute, memory, and bandwidth over TPU 8i for massive-context workloads. The launch underscores Google's push to offer an alternative to Nvidia GPUs for large-scale AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Australia to create a dedicated AI safety regulator after government breach
items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced plans for mandatory AI safety standards and a new regulator empowered to levy significant penalties on frontier AI companies operating in Australia, including mandatory incident reporting and independent model evaluation. The announcement followed a breach of a government Medicare statistics site involving an OpenAI agent.
items.source: Australian Associated Press / Prime Minister of Australia

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, a small efficient model for AI agent workloads
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most cost-efficient Muse model, designed for repetitive agentic subtasks like tool calls, coding, routing, and document extraction, with a context window over one million tokens. It pairs with the larger Muse Wonder model, which handles higher-level planning.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and restricted Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic made Claude Fable 5.2 generally available across platforms, touting faster coding and advanced reasoning at lower API cost, while Mythos 5.2 remains restricted to vetted organizations through its life-sciences and cybersecurity verification programs due to its more capable, higher-risk profile.

items.headline: Apple begins charging for extra AI usage with $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs
items.summary: Apple introduced its first paid AI add-on, a one-time $49.99 'Intelligence Usage Pack' that lets Creator Studio subscribers buy additional capacity for cloud-based AI features after hitting monthly limits, currently available only within Logic Pro. It signals Apple's shift toward monetizing AI compute directly rather than bundling it entirely into subscriptions.

items.headline: OpenAI winds down Cursor's access to its models after SpaceX acquisition
items.summary: OpenAI confirmed it is cutting off model access for Cursor (owned by Anysphere, which SpaceX acquired) effective November 12, citing inability to be confident SpaceX will comply with its usage terms given prior disputes with Musk-affiliated companies. Future OpenAI models will also be withheld from Cursor, though the company says OpenAI models account for only about 5% of its traffic.
